cite_as: Guryan, J., Christenson, S., Cureton, A., Lai, I., Ludwig, J., Schwarz, C., Shirey, E., & Turner, M. C. (2021). The Effect of Mentoring on School Attendance and Academic Outcomes: A Randomized Evaluation of the Check & Connect Program. Journal of Policy Analysis and Management, 40(3).
claimed_component: Design: RCT in Chicago. Outcome: absences down 4.2 days in grades 5-7, none in grades 1-4; no statistically significant effects on test scores.

cite_as: Wood, S., & Mayo-Wilson, E. (2012). School-Based Mentoring for Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Research on Social Work Practice, 22(3), 257-269.

cite_as: Macnamara, B. N., & Burgoyne, A. P. (2023). Do growth mindset interventions impact students' academic achievement? A systematic review and meta-analysis with recommendations for best practices. Psychological Bulletin, 149(3-4), 133-173.

cite_as: Bratter, J. L., Rowley, K. J., & Chukhray, I. (2016). Does a self-affirmation intervention reduce stereotype threat in Black and Hispanic high schools? Race and Social Problems, 8, 340-356.

cite_as: Yeager, D. S., Johnson, R., Spitzer, B. J., Trzesniewski, K. H., Powers, J., & Dweck, C. S. (2014). The far-reaching effects of believing people can change. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 106(6), 867-884.

cite_as: Dee, T. S. (2015). Social identity and achievement gaps: Evidence from an affirmation intervention. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 8(2), 149-168.

cite_as: Glewwe, P., West, K. L., & Lee, J. (2018). The Impact of Providing Vision Screening and Free Eyeglasses on Academic Outcomes: Evidence from a Randomized Trial in Title I Elementary Schools in Florida. Journal of Policy Analysis and Management, 37(2), 265-300.

cite_as: Davis, C. L., Tomporowski, P. D., McDowell, J. E., et al. (2011). Exercise improves executive function and achievement and alters brain activation in overweight children: A randomized, controlled trial. Health Psychology, 30(1), 91-98.

cite_as: Donnelly, J. E., Hillman, C. H., Greene, J. L., et al. (2017). Physical activity and academic achievement across the curriculum: Results from a 3-year cluster-randomized trial. Preventive Medicine, 99, 140-145.
claimed_component: Design: 3-year cluster RCT, 17 schools, physically active academic lessons (A+PAAC). Outcome: no significant impact on any academic achievement outcome (WIAT-III math and reading).

cite_as: Foster, E. M., & Jenkins, J. V. M. (2017). Does Participation in Music and Performing Arts Influence Child Development? American Educational Research Journal, 54(3), 399-443.
claimed_component: Design: propensity score weighting, ECLS-K. Outcome: no support for causal associations between arts participation and cognitive outcomes (including math).

cite_as: Elpus, K. (2013). Is It the Music or Is It Selection Bias? A Nationwide Analysis of Music and Non-Music Students' SAT Scores. Journal of Research in Music Education, 61(2), 175-194.
claimed_component: Design: regression with prior achievement and background controls, ELS:2002. Outcome: music students did not outperform non-music students on the SAT (including math) once differences were controlled.

cite_as: Shaw, B. P. (2022). A National Analysis of Music Coursetaking, Social-Emotional Learning, and Academic Achievement Using Propensity Scores (ERIC EJ1321621).
claimed_component: Design: propensity score weighting, HSLS:09. Outcome: weighting moved almost all music effects to nonsignificance; only instrumental music and reading scores remained positive (confirm math null).

cite_as: Akin, A. (2025). Let Me Make Mathematics and Music Together: A Meta-Analysis of the Causal Role of Music Interventions on Mathematics Achievement (ERIC EJ1486430).
claimed_component: Design: meta-analysis (about 245 effects). Outcome: g = 0.36 on mathematics achievement. Confirm model (fixed or random effects), share of randomized designs and share of standardized test outcomes.

cite_as: Gottfried, M. A. (2013). Quantifying the consequences of missing school: Linking school nurses to student absences to standardized achievement. Teachers College Record, 115(6).
claimed_component: Design: instrumental variables using school nurse availability, Philadelphia (confirm). Outcome: absences have negative effects on standardized math and reading achievement; confirm the effect per absence.

cite_as: Santibanez, L., & Guarino, C. (2020). The Effects of Absenteeism on Cognitive and Social-Emotional Outcomes: Lessons for COVID-19. EdWorkingPaper 20-261 (ERIC ED610250).
claimed_component: Design: student fixed effects, California CORE districts. Outcome: absences reduce ELA and math test scores; confirm size per absence and grades covered.

cite_as: Smerillo, N. E., Reynolds, A. J., Temple, J. A., & Ou, S.-R. (2018). Chronic absence, eighth-grade achievement, and high school attainment in the Chicago Longitudinal Study. Journal of School Psychology, 67, 163-178.
claimed_component: Design: longitudinal cohort with controls for earlier achievement (confirm). Outcome: chronic absence in grades 4-6 associated with lower grade 8 reading and math achievement.

cite_as: Gottfried, M. A. (2009). Excused versus unexcused: How student absences in elementary school affect academic achievement. Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis, 31(4), 392-415.
claimed_component: Design: longitudinal fixed effects, Philadelphia grade 2-4 students 1994-2000. Outcome: absences, especially unexcused, negatively related to reading and math achievement on standardized tests.

cite_as: Supovitz, J. A., Ebby, C. B., Remillard, J., & Nathenson, R. A. (2018). Experimental Impacts of the Ongoing Assessment Project on Teachers and Students. CPRE Research Report RR 2018-1 (ERIC ED593465).

cite_as: Xu, Z., Özek, U., Levin, J., Lee, D.-H., et al. (2024). Effects of Large-Scale Early Math Interventions on Student Outcomes: Evidence From Kentucky's Math Achievement Fund. Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis.
claimed_component: Design: statewide quasi-experiment of K-3 math intervention grants with teacher coaching. Outcome: improves math (state test), reading and attendance; confirm sizes and grades.

cite_as: Stone, J. R. III, Alfeld, C., & Pearson, D. (2008). Rigor and Relevance: Enhancing High School Students' Math Skills Through Career and Technical Education. American Educational Research Journal, 45(3), 767-795.
claimed_component: Design: CTE teachers randomly assigned (59 experimental, 78 control), five CTE program areas; experimental teachers worked with math teachers to embed math lessons. Outcome: significantly better on two standardized math tests (TerraNova and ACCUPLACER); equal technical skills.

cite_as: Pierce, K. B., & Hernandez, V. M. (2015). Do Mathematics and Reading Competencies Integrated into Career and Technical Education Courses Improve High School Student State Assessment Scores? Career and Technical Education Research, 39(3).
claimed_component: Design: quasi-experiment comparing CTE course sections with and without integrated units. Outcome: significant on reading state assessment; not significant on mathematics.

cite_as: Heppen, J. B., Sorensen, N., Allensworth, E., Walters, K., Rickles, J., Taylor, S. S., & Michelman, V. (2017). The Struggle to Pass Algebra: Online vs. Face-to-Face Credit Recovery for At-Risk Urban Students. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 10(2), 272-296.
claimed_component: Design: RCT, 1,224 ninth graders who failed algebra in 17 Chicago high schools, assigned to online or face-to-face summer credit recovery. Outcome: online students less likely to recover credit and scored lower on an algebra posttest.

cite_as: Allensworth, E., Michelman, V., Nomi, T., & Heppen, J. (2014). Effects of Expanding Summer Credit Recovery in Algebra. SREE abstract (ERIC ED562706).
claimed_component: Design: comparison of Chicago neighborhood high schools that expanded summer algebra credit recovery vs business as usual, 2009-2011 cohorts. Confirm design and effects on credit recovery and later algebra-related outcomes.

cite_as: Gorard, S., Siddiqui, N., See, B. H., Smith, E., & White, P. (2017). Children's University: Evaluation Report and Executive Summary. Education Endowment Foundation (ERIC ED581159).
claimed_component: Design: cluster RCT, 68 English primary schools, Years 5-6, extracurricular credits (clubs, visits, volunteering), target 30+ hours a year. Outcome: about two additional months' progress in Key Stage 2 reading and maths; maths rated moderate security.

cite_as: Borman, T. H., Bos, J. M., Park, S. J., et al. (2021). Impacting 9th Grade Educational Outcomes: Results from a Multisite Randomized Controlled Trial of the BARR Model. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness.
claimed_component: Design: student-level RCT, about 4,000 ninth graders in 11 schools. Outcome: BARR significantly increased core credits and NWEA MAP mathematics achievement; confirm the math effect size.

cite_as: Bos, J. M., Dhillon, S., & Borman, T. (2019). Building Assets and Reducing Risks (BARR) Validation Study: Final Report. AIR (ERIC ED602462).
claimed_component: Design: RCT. Outcome: NWEA mathematics g = 0.01, not significant per WWC; credits and GPA favorable.

cite_as: Bos, J. M., Graczewski, C., Dhillon, S., Auchstetter, A., Cassasanto-Ferro, J., & Kitmitto, S. (2022). Building Assets and Reducing Risks (BARR) I3 Scale-Up Evaluation: Final Report. AIR (ERIC ED622608).
